items.headline: Eisenkot leads challenge to Netanyahu as Israel votes
items.summary: Former Israeli general Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a leading challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Tuesday's election. TIME interviewed Eisenkot, and The Nation examined the opposition's positions in the run-up to the vote.

items.headline: DOJ sues to block Alaska Senate certification
items.summary: The Justice Department sued to block certification of Alaska’s Senate result if the Republican incumbent loses, citing possible confusion between two candidates named Dan Sullivan. One is the GOP senator; Republicans accuse the other, a retired schoolteacher, of being a Democratic plant.

items.headline: Hundreds of thousands protest across Europe
items.summary: More than 400,000 people rallied across France over school funding and living costs, and police made nearly 1,000 arrests after clashes in Paris. Large demonstrations also drew crowds in Milan, Rome, Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.

items.headline: U.S. cuts embassy staff over Iran threats
items.summary: The U.S. is reducing staffing at four Middle East embassies over increased threats from Iran. A memo from the Director of National Intelligence to Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran has substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel.

items.headline: Trump's Latino support slips in Florida
items.summary: Polls show growing frustration with President Trump among Latino voters. TIME examines whether Democrats can turn that discontent into votes in Florida’s midterm races.

items.headline: DOJ orders California counties to set aside some ballots
items.summary: The Justice Department sent letters ordering some California counties to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizens. The move is the latest escalation in its legal battle with the state.

items.headline: Starlink service restored in Ukraine
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said normal Starlink operating speeds were restored on Saturday. The service had been disrupted for more than a week.

items.headline: N.Y. Archdiocese agrees to $800M abuse settlement
items.summary: The Archdiocese of New York agreed to an $800 million settlement over sexual abuse claims against clergy and lay workers. All 1,300 survivors have agreed to the deal, according to an attorney for some plaintiffs.

items.headline: Trump exempts some Canadian imports from tariffs
items.summary: President Trump exempted some Canadian imports from his 50% tariffs in a move aimed at helping Sen. Susan Collins in Maine. Collins, in a tight race with Democrat Troy Jackson, said she raised the tariffs’ toll on Maine families and businesses with trade officials.

items.headline: Toxic metals found in Lahaina fire survivors
items.summary: Testing found high levels of arsenic and other toxic metals in the bodies of Lahaina residents more than a year after the wildfire destroyed the Maui town. Yale Environment 360 reported the findings on Oct. 23.

digest.overview:
President Trump rallied Sunday in Port Huron, Michigan, for Republicans Mike Rogers and John James, while Barack Obama and Bernie Sanders campaigned there for Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms. The Justice Department has sued to block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses to Mary Peltola, citing a second candidate also named Dan Sullivan; Trump said he directed the suit. The department also ordered some California counties to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizens. Trump said he is weighing a deal with Iran or action to "finish them off" as the U.S. cut staff at four Middle East embassies over Iranian threats. The Archdiocese of New York agreed to an $800 million settlement with 1,300 survivors of clergy sexual abuse.

Abroad, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's runoff with 51.76% of valid votes to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.24%, securing a fourth term, but Bolsonaro refused to concede and said he would seek to annul the result. Israelis vote Tuesday after a final Maariv poll gave neither Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition the 61 seats needed for a majority. Houthi rebels fired missiles at Riyadh's airport hours after it reopened. Russia launched 140 drones and four missiles at Ukraine overnight, and Ukraine said 115 targets were downed or suppressed. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić conceded that his list lost parliamentary elections to a student-led movement. In China, Kim Jong Un met Wang Huning rather than Xi Jinping during the North Korean leader's first visit in a year. Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado made a surprise return home after more than 10 months abroad.

home.overview:
Seattle smothered Patrick Mahomes, holding him to 44 passing yards in a 20–3 Sunday-night win that handed Kansas City its first loss, and Minnesota beat Indianapolis 16–10 to stand alone as the NFL's last unbeaten team at 6–0. Atlanta forced four turnovers to beat San Francisco 29–20, Cincinnati scored 35 straight points to rout Baltimore 35–13, and J.J. McCarthy won his first Giants start 27–21 in overtime at Houston; Cowboys at Eagles closes Week 7 tonight. Luka Dončić scored 52 as the Lakers rallied past Utah 132–123 to reach 3–0, the defending-champion Knicks fell to 0–3, and Oklahoma City lost Jalen Williams to a leg injury in a win over the Clippers. The World Series resumes tonight in Tampa Bay with Milwaukee up 2–0.

Kylian Mbappé struck twice as Real Madrid won El Clásico 2–1 at Camp Nou, handing Barcelona their first league loss and cutting the gap to three points. Liverpool beat Brighton 2–0, Bournemouth won 3–0 at Old Trafford, and Bayern won 3–1 at Freiburg to go top of the Bundesliga before Saturday's Klassiker with Dortmund. Rennes lead Ligue 1 ahead of PSG–Lyon tonight, the Carabao Cup fourth round starts Tuesday, and Suwon Samsung moved eight points clear in K League 2. In the KBO, Kia and Samsung finally opened their second-round series Monday night in Daegu.

brief: Kia and Samsung opened their best-of-five second-round series Monday night in Daegu after Sunday’s rainout.
Chris Paddack started for Samsung against Kia's James Naile in a matchup of American aces.
Samsung's manager acknowledged that the rainout erased his team's rest advantage over Kia.
Kia catcher Kim Tae-gun returns to Daegu, where he hit a grand slam in the 2024 Korean Series.
Game 2 is Tuesday in Daegu and Game 3 Thursday in Gwangju; the winner meets regular-season champion KT Wiz in the Korean Series.
